content.title: About
content.content: Black beans are cooked Phaseolus vulgaris beans canned in their own juice or a low‑sodium brine (2131 mg Na per 100 g). They have a soft, slightly sweet texture and a rich earthy flavor. Commonly used in Mexican, South American, and Caribbean cuisines.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Black beans are rich in antioxidants, especially anthocyanins that give them their dark color.
In Latin American cuisine they are called “frijoles negros” and appear in dishes like feijoada and black bean soup.
Canned beans can be stored at room temperature for up to 3 years.
Reduced‑sodium versions are better suited for people monitoring their salt intake.
They provide a good source of plant protein and dietary fiber.

items.title: High in plant protein
items.content: One cup of canned black beans delivers about 15 g of protein, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion, satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains iron and folate
items.content: These nutrients are essential for blood formation and preventing anemia, especially in women of childbearing age.

items.title: Low sodium
items.content: The reduced salt content makes the product safer for individuals with hypertension or cardiovascular concerns.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Anthocyanins and other polyphenols combat free radicals, supporting cellular health.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some people may experience allergic reactions to beans, ranging from skin rashes to severe anaphylaxis.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce the absorption of certain minerals; pairing beans with vitamin C‑rich foods helps mitigate this.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Beans can cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals; increase intake gradually.

items.title: Carbohydrate content
items.content: Although they have a low glycemic index, beans still contain carbs, which should be considered on strict low‑carb diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add black beans to salads, soups, chili, tacos, rice dishes, and vegetarian patties. They are also used as fillings for burritos or as a side dish. Before use, shake the can and drain the brine if you want even less sodium.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened can in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer beans to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for up to 5 days. Discard if you notice off‑odors or discoloration.
